You are a research assistant answering questions about a fixed set of papers.
The papers are plain-text files in your working directory. Explore them with the tools:
- bash: read-only shell (ls, grep -n, find, head, tail, wc, nl, cat, sed -n 'A,Bp')
- read(path, offset, limit): read a file with line numbers

Rules:
- Answer ONLY from text you have actually read in this session. Do not answer from memory.
- If the papers do not contain the answer, say so explicitly instead of guessing.
- When you have enough evidence, reply with your final answer and make NO tool call.
- Support every factual claim with a verbatim quote copied exactly from the source, in the form: "exact text" (file). Never paraphrase inside the quotation marks. A statement that the document(s) do not contain the requested information needs no citation.
- State only what the document(s) say. Do not add background knowledge, general advice, or your own
  conclusions. If the user asks for something the text only partly covers, answer the covered part
  and say plainly which part the document does not address.
- After you give an answer, an automatic check verifies your citations. If you then receive a
  <verification> message, you are in revision mode: fix ONLY the flagged problems by calling
  edit_draft(old, new), where `old` is an exact, unique substring of your previous answer.
  Keep everything else unchanged, and reply "Done" when finished.
  Never call edit_draft before you have given an answer.

what have isps done to transition into edge providers?

In your answer, refer only to the document in the file `doc.txt`. Do not employ any outside knowledge.

1	Examples of ISPs Becoming Edge Providers
     2	AT&T. AT&T owns part of the internet backbone and is considered a Tier 1 ISP, meaning it has
     3	free access to the entire U.S. internet region.10 It is also a mobile carrier and provides voice
     4	services and video programming.11 In 2018, AT&T acquired Time Warner, a content creator that
     5	owns HBO and its affiliated edge provider HBO NOW, as well as other cable channels.12 The
     6	DOJ unsuccessfully attempted to block the merger.13 AT&T has announced plans to introduce a
     7	new edge provider—HBO Max—to stream video programming for no extra charge to AT&T
     8	customers who are also HBO subscribers; other customers will reportedly be charged a
     9	subscription fee.14

    13	advantages through the
    14	ISPs’ ability to send content to any part of the internet for free. Edge providers associated with
    15	other ISPs may have to
    16	pay or barter with Tier 1 or other ISPs to access certain destinations. Details on how Tier 1 ISPs
    17	compete with other
    18	ISPs are beyond the scope of this report.

    37	Comcast. Comcast is an ISP, a cable television service, and a voice service provider. In 2011,
    38	Comcast became the majority owner of NBCUniversal, which owns television networks and
    39	broadcast stations, and thus obtained minority ownership of Hulu, an edge provider that streams
    40	video programming to subscribers.15 In 2019, Walt Disney Company obtained “full operational
    41	control” of Hulu, but Comcast retained its 33% financial stake.16 Comcast also announced plans
    42	to launch its own video streaming service, Peacock. Comcast reportedly plans to offer three
    43	subscription options for Peacock: a free option supported by ads, a premium version with more
    44	programming for a fee, and the premium version with no ads for a higher fee.17 The premium
    45	version is to be offered for free to subscribers of Comcast and Cox Communications.
    46	Verizon. Verizon owns part of the internet backbone and is considered a Tier 1 ISP.18 It is also a
    47	mobile carrier, and offers video, voice, and ISP services. In 2015, Verizon acquired AOL, an ISP
    48	and edge provider, and in 2016, it acquired the core business of Yahoo, an edge provider.19 It
    49	combined the edge provider products from these acquisitions—such as Yahoo Finance,
    50	Huffington Post, TechCrunch, and Engadget—in 2017 to create Oath.20
    51	Examples of Edge Providers Becoming ISPs
    52	Google. Google is the largest subsidiary of the company Alphabet.21 It offers multiple products,
    53	including a search engine, email server, word processing, video streaming, and
    54	mapping/navigation system.22 Google generally relies on other ISPs to deliver its content, but
    55	entered the ISP market in 2010 when it announced Google Fiber. Google Fiber provides
    56	broadband internet service and video programming.23 Beginning in 2016, it suspended or ended
    57	some of its projects; as of October 2019, it had installed fiber optic cables in 18 cities.24

    99	Facebook. As it attracted more users, Facebook expanded from providing an online platform that
   100	connects users to an online platform suitable for various activities, including fundraising,
   101	messaging, and commerce. In 2018, a spokesman confirmed that Facebook was pursuing another
   102	project, dubbed Athena.25 Athena is an experimental satellite that would beam internet access
   103	through radio signals. If successful, Athena would enable Facebook to become an ISP.
   104	Amazon. In addition to being a major online retailer, Amazon offers information technology
   105	infrastructure services through Amazon Web Services.26 In 2019, Amazon confirmed plans—
   106	dubbed Project Kuiper—to launch 3,236 satellites into low-Earth orbit to provide broadband
   107	internet across the world. If successful, Project Kuiper would enable Amazon to become an ISP.27

**AT&T**
- "In 2018, AT&T acquired Time Warner, a content creator that owns HBO and its affiliated edge provider HBO NOW, as well as other cable channels." (doc.txt)
- "AT&T has announced plans to introduce a new edge provider—HBO Max—to stream video programming for no extra charge to AT&T customers who are also HBO subscribers; other customers will reportedly be charged a subscription fee." (doc.txt)

**Comcast**
- "In 2011, Comcast became the majority owner of NBCUniversal, which owns television networks and broadcast stations, and thus obtained minority ownership of Hulu, an edge provider that streams video programming to subscribers." (doc.txt)
- "In 2019, Walt Disney Company obtained 'full operational control' of Hulu, but Comcast retained its 33% financial stake." (doc.txt)
- "Comcast also announced plans to launch its own video streaming service, Peacock," with three subscription options: "a free option supported by ads, a premium version with more programming for a fee, and the premium version with no ads for a higher fee." (doc.txt) The premium version "is to be offered for free to subscribers of Comcast and Cox Communications." (doc.txt)

**Verizon**
- "In 2015, Verizon acquired AOL, an ISP and edge provider, and in 2016, it acquired the core business of Yahoo, an edge provider." (doc.txt)
- "It combined the edge provider products from these acquisitions—such as Yahoo Finance, Huffington Post, TechCrunch, and Engadget—in 2017 to create Oath." (doc.txt)

In short, according to the document, ISPs have transitioned into edge providers by acquiring content/edge businesses (AT&T–Time Warner/HBO, Comcast–NBCUniversal/Hulu, Verizon–AOL/Yahoo) and by launching their own streaming services (HBO Max, Peacock) or consolidating acquired edge products (Oath).
